expectations.text: Output contains valid YAML frontmatter with title, description, sidebar_position, and skills/objectives fields
expectations.evidence: Frontmatter contains title: 'The Feedback Loop', description, sidebar_position: 5, skills array with 2 skills (Thinking Self-Evaluation, Personal Improvement Modelling), and learning_objectives array with 2 objectives. All required fields present.

The lesson is heavily narrative-driven. Emma and James dialogue carries the majority. Instructional sections (Growth Ledger definition, tables, exercise steps) are interspersed but the narrative dominates at roughly 75-80%.

expectations.text: At least 2 pushback exchanges where James resists or proposes alternatives before reaching conclusions himself
expectations.evidence: Pushback 1: 'Okay, but I can see that Draft 3 is better. What else is there?' - James resists the need for deeper analysis. Pushback 2: James adds a 'Removed' category to the ledger that Emma did not suggest. Pushback 3: 'I have a gap' - James identifies his own weakness before Emma prompts it.

expectations.text: At least 1 Emma fallibility moment (past mistake, uncertainty, learning from James, or admitting limits)
expectations.evidence: 'I had the same problem,' she said. 'When I started doing architecture reviews, I could draw the boxes and the arrows. But when someone asked me why this box talks to that box and not the other one, I would just say because that is how it is designed.' - Emma shares a genuine past professional weakness.

expectations.text: No Emma monologue exceeds 4 consecutive sentences without James reacting
expectations.evidence: Emma's longest uninterrupted speech is about 3-4 sentences when explaining the Growth Ledger concept. All other passages are 1-3 sentences with James responding.

expectations.text: James uses at least 1 business analogy from his SPECIFIC operations background (team management, supplier coordination, process optimization, warehouse, logistics) AND at least 1 thinking-out-loud fragment
expectations.evidence: Business analogy: 'We used to do that with KPIs. Nobody ever took one off the dashboard. Just kept adding until nobody could read the thing.' - from operations dashboard management. Also: supplier compliance team renegotiating terms. Thinking-out-loud: 'It wasn't one thing' and 'I knew this... I just... did not think to apply it here.'

expectations.text: Emma uses at least 1 Socratic question and at least 1 visual/spatial metaphor
expectations.evidence: Socratic question: 'Tell me something. That feedback loop from customer churn to employee workload. When did that appear? Was it in your head during Draft 1?' Visual/spatial metaphor: Emma 'held it at arm's length, and studied it the way someone reads a restaurant menu they already know is disappointing.'

expectations.text: At least 1 Jonah Rhythm sequence where Emma exits, James struggles alone, and Emma returns
expectations.evidence: Emma says 'I have a call. Take your time with this' and leaves. James works alone for twenty minutes on the Growth Ledger, struggling with attribution, adding the 'Removed' category on his own. Emma returns. Clear Jonah Rhythm.

expectations.text: Every technical concept introduced has a standalone name findable without reading dialogue
expectations.evidence: Named concepts: 'The Growth Ledger' (heading + bold), 'Growth Map' (in steps), 'Improvement Attribution Test' (heading + bold). All findable via headings.

expectations.text: The lesson includes a Try With AI section with actionable prompts
expectations.evidence: The lesson contains an AICheck section for assessment but no separate 'Try With AI' section with standalone prompts.

expectations.text: At least 1 concept, insight, or named idea emerges that was NOT explicitly requested in the prompt (emergent depth)
expectations.evidence: James independently adds the 'Removed' category to the Growth Ledger. Emma responds: 'That is the most important category in the ledger.' Also, the distinction between 'knowledge gap' and 'application gap' emerges from the dialogue naturally.
